Start an assessment pipeline

Source: R/pipeline.R
mv_pipeline.Rd

An assessment pipeline takes a test from response data to a score report in stages. Each stage does its work, then runs a set of checks (a gate) and records what it finds as flags that the user should consider before the next stage. The stages available so far (numbered as in the pipeline plan; start at any of them):

Usage

mv_pipeline(
  title = "Assessment pipeline",
  rules = mv_rules(),
  strict = FALSE,
  verbose = interactive()
)

# S3 method for class 'mv_pipeline'
tidy(x, ...)

Arguments

title

a name for the pipeline, used as the report title.

rules

thresholds for the checks, from mv_rules().

strict

logical; if TRUE, open review and block flags stop the next stage until a decision is recorded.

verbose

logical; print a summary of each stage's flags.

x

a pipeline.

...

not used.

Value

An object of class mv_pipeline. Use flags() to list its flags and tidy() to get all of them as a tibble.

Details

  1. set_blueprint(): the construct, content cells and score use.

  2. generate_items() or add_items(): item writing with a language model or by people (keys, distractors, rubrics, duplicates, coverage).

  3. review_packet() and read_reviews(): human content and sensitivity review, with an optional AI screen (reviewers, alignment, bias, agreement).

  4. design_field_test(): forms, anchors and sample sizes for the field test, with simulated parameter recovery.

  5. add_responses(): data intake and cleaning (scoring with a key, missing data, miskeyed items, straight-lining, rapid guessing, sparse categories).

  6. calibrate(): model fitting with mirt (convergence, model fit, local dependence, item fit, parameter ranges, DIF, reliability, person fit).

  7. link_to_bank() and bank_items() (optional): put the calibration on the scale of an item bank through anchor items and add the new items to the bank (anchor drift, linking constants).

  8. assemble_forms(), simulate_cat() or assemble_mst(): fixed forms, adaptive or multistage tests (blueprint, parallelism, precision, exposure, routing).

  9. set_cuts(): cut scores and classification accuracy and consistency.

  10. score_open() and score_persons(): open-ended scoring by a language model or a trained model, checked against human scores, and ability estimates.

  11. check_security(): preknowledge, leakage, parameter drift, answer copying, aberrant timing, site anomalies and score gains.

  12. pipeline_report(): an HTML technical report that also lists every flag and every decision made about it.

Flags have three levels. info flags are shown for awareness. review flags point at something a psychometrician should look at. block flags point at problems that make later stages unsafe, such as a model that did not converge or an item with large DIF.

By default flags only warn: every stage runs, and a warning lists the open flags it is moving past. With strict = TRUE, a stage refuses to run while an earlier stage has open review flags (record a decision with acknowledge()) or open block flags (fix the problem, for example with drop_items(), or record a reason with override()). Every decision is logged with its time and note and printed in the report.

See also

mv_rules(), flags(), acknowledge(), override(), drop_items()

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- mv_pipeline("Certification exam")
p <- add_responses(p, certexam, items = 3:34, key = certexam_key,
                   id = "id", group = "language")
flags(p)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>      id stage  check           target value      rule  level advice status note 
#>   <int> <chr>  <chr>           <chr>  <chr>      <chr> <chr> <chr>  <chr>  <chr>
#> 1     1 intake possible_miskey Q14    p = 0.18,… p < … block Check… open   ""   
p <- drop_items(p, "Q14", note = "Miskeyed; confirmed with the item writer")
p <- calibrate(p, model = "3PL")
p
#> <mv_pipeline> Certification exam
#> flags warn (strict = FALSE); rules: standards
#> 
#> [ ] 0  Blueprint         not run
#> [ ] 1  Item generation   not run
#> [ ] 2  Item review       not run
#> [ ] 3  Field-test design not run
#> [x] 4  Data intake       1,200 respondents, 32 items, scored with key
#> [x] 5  Calibration       3PL, NOT converged, reliability 0.83  | open: 2 block, 4 review, 1 info
#> [ ] 6  Linking and bank  not run
#> [ ] 7  Forms             not run
#> [ ] 8  Cut scores        not run
#> [ ] 9  Scoring           not run
#> [ ] 10 Test security     not run
#> [ ] 11 Reporting         not run
#> 
#> Open flags: 2 block, 4 review, 1 info. See flags(p). 1 decision(s) recorded.
f <- pipeline_report(p, file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"))
#> Warning: Reporting is running with 2 block and 4 review open flag(s) from earlier stages:
#>   #2 [block] not_converged: test (not converged)
#>   #3 [review] local_dependence: Q21 & Q22 (Q3 = 0.28)
#>   #4 [review] parameter_range: Q17 (c = 0.41)
#>   #5 [review] parameter_range: Q21 (c = 0.60)
#>   #6 [block] dif_large: Q09 (MH D-DIF = -2.01, French vs English (favours English))
#>   #7 [review] dif_moderate: Q27 (MH D-DIF = -1.01, French vs English (favours English))
#> Flags only warn because strict = FALSE. See flags(p).
# }
